scientific_hypothesis: Applying ±1.5 nm bounded mutations to the convergent layer thickness bands from iteration 06, combined with random perturbations to non-convergent layers, will increase best_target_score by at least 0.02 without reducing tightest_margin below the previous round's value.
expected_advantages: Preserves the spectral balance achieved in iteration 06 while exploring local improvements
Bounded mutations prevent divergence from the promising region of design space
Diversity injection prevents premature convergence to a single local optimum
known_risks: I am uncertain whether ±1.5 nm is the optimal mutation bound for this wavelength separation; literature on HfO2/SiO2 dual-band filter sensitivity would confirm this
I recall that HfO2 has higher extinction in deep UV but am uncertain of the exact cutoff; the material dataset will provide measured values
The 20-layer count was chosen based on iteration 06 performance, not from a systematic layer-count study; a different count might perform better but that would be a different axis
I am not certain whether the alternating HfO2-first sequence is optimal versus SiO2-first; this route does not test that hypothesis
expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should increase relative to iteration 06's 0.8206 while tightest_margin should not decrease
If the hypothesis does not hold, best_target_score will remain within 0.01 of iteration 06's value or tightest_margin will fall
valid_candidates count should remain comparable to iteration 06's 9 physically valid candidates
thicknesses_nm should show bounded variation around the iteration 06 convergent values for even-indexed layers
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 0.01 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat this axis as exhausted and stop, keeping the current best
If tightest_margin falls below 0.40 for three consecutive rounds, relax the mutation bound from ±1.5 nm to ±2.0 nm and continue
If valid_candidates drops below 5 for two consecutive rounds, reduce the random perturbation magnitude for odd-indexed layers and continue
